evidence: mux.lisp:813-817 `(:admit (setf (fnn-mux-conn-hs-id conn) x) (when queuedp (setf (fnn-mux-loop-waiting loop) (delete conn ...))) (fnn-mux-start-handshake loop conn ms)` with no phase reset, while mux.lisp:833-836 evaluates `(fnn-tls-accept-begin ...)` before setting `phase :handshake`. On the error path, mux.lisp:278-283 runs `(when (fnn-mux-conn-hs-id conn) (fnn-mux-handshake-release ...)) (when (member was '(:tls-queued :hs-wait)) ... 'fn-owner-handshake-leave ...)`. Compare the :refuse branch at 825-827 ('ACL2 counted it out of the waiting already', phase set to :new) and the queued-implicit :admit at 858-861, which also sets phase :new first.
fix: Set `(fnn-mux-conn-phase conn) :new` in the :admit branch before calling fnn-mux-start-handshake, as the queued-implicit branch does.
reviewer: fn-hsb-admit with queuedp already decrements waiting on :admit: left = waiting-1 is stored in the :admit state (books/tls-handshake-decision.lisp:335, 349-351). fnn-mux-request-handshake's :admit branch leaves phase :hs-wait (mux.lisp:813-817). fnn-mux-start-handshake evaluates fnn-tls-accept-begin before setting phase :handshake (mux.lisp:833-836), so a signal from SSL_new/SSL_set_fd reaches fnn-mux-guarded -> fnn-mux-finish with was=:hs-wait. Finish then calls fn-owner-handshake-leave, decrementing waiting a second time (fn-hsb-leave, books/tls-handshake-decision.lisp:370-374). It uses nfix, so this is undercounting, not a fault. It is reachable only when accept-begin fails (resource exhaustion), so low.
scenario: A STARTTLS upgrade waits (:hs-wait), and a later pass admits it with queuedp=t, which tells ACL2 it left the waiting count. SSL_new or SSL_set_fd then fails in fnn-tls-accept-begin and signals. fnn-mux-guarded calls fnn-mux-finish with phase still :hs-wait, so it reports both fn-owner-handshake-done and fn-owner-handshake-leave. The node's waiting count is decremented for a socket that no longer waits, which weakens the 'refused busy when too many wait' bound, or faults if ACL2 refuses the underflow.
title: STARTTLS admitted from the wait queue keeps phase :hs-wait, so a failure in fnn-tls-accept-begin double-counts the handshake leave
